### Fidelity diagnostics: report the centroid of mismatching pixels (planned 2026-11-02 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-02 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Locate the spatial centre of scattered rendering errors without treating their enclosing rectangle's midpoint as their centre. `tools/fidelity_spatial.py` reports row/column counts, bounds and runs; searches found no mismatch-centroid diagnostic.

**Implemented.** Added opt-in `--difference-centroid`, a constant-space row-major scan using the existing raw RGBA predicate, crop-relative mean coordinates, explicit JSON/text null for no mismatches, tests, and documentation. The test fixture covers unequal mismatch magnitudes, tolerance exclusion, hidden RGB and opaque-alpha fallback; CLI coverage checks cropped coordinates, both verdict outcomes, and default omission. (planned 2026-11-02 by the plan role; completed within this run.)

### Reference-pixel histogram: report each emitted color's centroid (planned 2026-11-02 by the plan role; done 2026-11-02 by the feature role)

**Goal and grounding.** Report the spatial centre of several palette colors in one reference region without repeating single-color searches. The histogram result counts colors and can traverse coordinates for bounds and first positions; search reports already support a centroid for one target. The histogram option adds the corresponding multi-color diagnostic.

**Implementation.** Added `--color-centroids` in `tools/sample_arguments.py`, requiring `--histogram` before image reads. The histogram result accumulates integer x/y sums for emitted colors during its positioned traversal and divides by each color's full-region count. JSON and text report absolute pixel-index means without a half-pixel offset, grouping by RGB normally and RGBA with `--alpha`. Top-color limits retain all occurrences of emitted colors without per-color rescans or stored coordinate lists. The option and invariant are documented in README.md and docs/invariants.md.

**Verification.** `tests/test_sample_histogram_centroids.py` covers cropped means in text and JSON, top-color contributor retention, RGB/RGBA grouping, one shared positioned traversal, default omission, validation before image reads, and package/direct-script parity. `make check` was run after implementation.

### Shared stylesheet parser: preserve escaped whitespace at value boundaries (planned 2026-11-01 by the plan role; independent of the completed ASCII priority-keyword change) — done 2026-11-01 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Keep the GTK/Firefox test reader from dropping an escaped terminal character. Reproduced 2026-11-01: a custom-property value consisting of `token`, a backslash and a space returns just `token` and the backslash; a backslash followed by a tab loses the tab too. In `tests/support/gtk_css.py::parse_css`, the declaration is split from `chunk.strip(' \t\n\r\f')`, which deletes the character before `_collapse_whitespace` can preserve its escape. The finished non-CSS boundary plan explicitly excludes escaped CSS whitespace; the archived interior-normalization plans retain the escape scanner but do not address this earlier trim.

**Approach and files.** Keep the trimmed declaration for empty-chunk detection and diagnostics, but split the original `chunk` at its first colon when extracting name and value. Let the existing `_collapse_whitespace` scanner normalize those original substrings so it can distinguish escaped characters from removable boundary whitespace. Add table-driven regressions in `tests/test_gtk_css.py::TestRuleBlockSemantics`, including `test_escaped_trailing_value_whitespace_is_preserved`, and extend the declaration-boundary guarantee in `docs/invariants.md` with the test names and implementation date. This is one three-file run; the completed ASCII priority-keyword change touches `_IMPORTANT_SUFFIX`, a separate operation; retain the current scanner's literal escape representation without introducing CSS escape decoding, newline-continuation handling or general syntax validation.

**Acceptance criteria.** Through `parse_css`, custom-property values ending in a backslash plus space or tab retain both characters, with and without additional unescaped boundary spaces, both before a semicolon and before the closing brace without a final semicolon. In semicolon cases, the following `color` declaration and selector list remain correct. Cover one and three consecutive backslashes (the final whitespace is escaped) and two backslashes (the unescaped boundary whitespace disappears). Ordinary unescaped spaces/tabs still disappear; a quoted terminal space, non-CSS boundary characters, empty declaration chunks, empty values and source-prefixed malformed-declaration diagnostics retain their existing behavior. Add named tests for these cases, preserve the public return shape and priority merge behavior, and run `make check`. No shipped artwork or stylesheet values change.

### Shared stylesheet parser: preserve non-CSS spacing at declaration boundaries (planned 2026-11-01 by the plan role; independent of the waiting priority-token separator plan) — done 2026-11-01 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Keep the GTK/Firefox test reader from silently discarding literal declaration characters. Reproduced 2026-11-01: `parse_css('a { content: token\u00a0; }')` returns `token` without the trailing U+00A0, and a declaration chunk containing just U+00A0 is ignored. In `tests/support/gtk_css.py::parse_css`, `chunk.strip()` removes Unicode whitespace before `_collapse_whitespace` sees it. The finished interior-normalization plans leave boundary trimming outside scope; the waiting priority plan changes `_IMPORTANT_SUFFIX`, not this call.

**Approach and files.** Change the declaration-chunk trim in `parse_css` to `chunk.strip(' \t\n\r\f')`. Retain the existing normalizer, malformed-declaration diagnostic and priority scanner. In `tests/test_gtk_css.py::TestRuleBlockSemantics`, add direct table-driven boundary regressions for U+00A0, U+2003 and U+000B, alongside `test_only_css_ascii_whitespace_collapses_between_tokens`. Extend the shared parser guarantee in `docs/invariants.md` with the new test names and implementation date. These three files form one small run. Priority suffixes, define-color parsing, escaped CSS whitespace and general CSS validation are outside scope; the waiting priority plan can merge in either order.

**Acceptance criteria.** For each listed character, unquoted values retain it at the beginning and end, including when surrounded by CSS whitespace; a value consisting solely of that character remains nonempty. A chunk containing solely that character and no colon raises the existing source-prefixed `ValueError` instead of disappearing. Empty chunks and chunks made solely of the five CSS whitespace characters remain ignored, and ordinary declaration boundary whitespace still disappears. Use ordinary values without priority suffixes so the regressions do not depend on the waiting plan. Existing quoted-value and malformed-declaration cases pass. No shipped stylesheet or visual value changes. Run `make check` after implementation.

Every stock arm that matches an icon-view node is a two-token spelling — class-only (`.view:*`) or element-only (`iconview:*`) — while the restated selectors below name element + class + states: strictly more matched tokens than every two-token twin (a strictly greater count wins at any source position), and an equal-token tie only against stock's class-only `:selected:focus` and `:backdrop:selected(:focus)` twins, where the sheet tail loses nothing because the stock theme resource loads first and the user sheet is appended after it in every cascade this theme ships (the same tail-order premise the landed selection and selected-row-button records state). ### Platinum GTK 4 push buttons: restate the stock checked hover and press compounds with the landed sunken face (planned 2026-10-31 by the plan role; independent of the re-filed GTK 3 plain-button shadows entry below — that entry touches only `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, a new `tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme::test_button_text_and_icon_shadows` beside `test_link_button_follows_the_button_state_rules` and its own `## gtk` invariants row, while this entry touches only `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, a new `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::TestGtk4Theme::test_button_checked_hover_and_active` beside `test_button_disabled_and_backdrop` and its own row, and no selector in either entry carries the other's sheet tokens, so every edit appends tail text plus one new test and one new invariants row and either queue order leaves the cascade and the tables right) — done 2026-11-02 by the clean role
— done 2026-10-31 by the feature role

**Goal.** On GTK 4, stock repaints a checked push button's face the moment it is hovered or pressed again: the toolkit resource `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Default/Default-light.css` in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-4.so.1` (libgtk-4 4.18.6, probed with `gresource` 2026-10-31, extraction verified under a scratch dir) declares `button:checked:hover { color: #2e3436; border-color: #cdc7c2; background-image: image(#d1ccc7); box-shadow: none; }` and `button:checked:active { color: #2e3436; border-color: #cdc7c2; background-image: image(#c8c2bc); box-shadow: none; }`. Both selectors outrank the landed `button:active, button:checked` sunken-bevel group by specificity, so any checked toggle-type button (toolbar toggle, check-armed button in a message dialog) that draws the theme's square sunken face flips to stock's rounded off-white face with no bevel on hover or press. No collected reference screenshot shows a GTK push button in a checked-and-hovered state, so this is a declaration-only platform adaptation reusing the landed face recipe.

**Grounding.** `grep -n "checked:hover\|checked:active" theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` matches only the landed `tab:checked:hover`, `switch:checked:hover` and `pathbar`/`stackswitcher` specific-selector arm rules — the plain `button:checked:hover` and `button:checked:active` selectors appear nowhere in either sheet, and no `PLANS.md` `## Planned` entry, `PLANS-DONE.md` finished record or `BUGS.md`/`BUGS-FIXED.md` heading names them (the landed GTK push-button disabled/backdrop and GTK 3 plain-button shadow entries both list them in their Scope boundaries as candidate plans of their own). GTK 3 stock has no such compounds: `grep -n "button:checked:hover\|button:checked:active"` over the extracted `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css` of `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0` (libgtk-3 3.24.49, probed 2026-10-31) returns nothing, so the GTK 3 sheet is untouched. The landed group these selectors lose to is `button:active, button:checked { box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #AAAAAA, inset -1px -1px #FFFFFF; }` pinned by the shared `tests/support/gtk_rule_cases.py::GtkSharedControlCases::test_button`; `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py` holds its bevel as `INVERTED_BUTTON_BEVEL`. `tests/support/gtk_css.py::parse_css` splits grouped selector lists into per-selector keys, and adding two selectors absent from the sheet creates two fresh per-selector dicts — no arrived state depends on whether some landed group has since gained keys, so the merge rule noted for the button-shadow entries never bites here.

**Approach and files.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, append at the sheet tail (after the landed paned directional block `paned.horizontal > separator:dir(ltr), paned.horizontal > separator:dir(rtl)` and whatever later entries land there) one dated (2026-10-31) comment naming the missing checked-hover reference surface, the GTK 4 probe above, and the landed `button:active, button:checked` group as the face source, then one group whose two members are each the exact stock twin so the appended later source order decides every tie: `button:checked:hover, button:checked:active` declaring exactly `background-image: none; border-color: #000000; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #AAAAAA, inset -1px -1px #FFFFFF; color: #000000`. The two members share one rule deliberately: they mean the same restated sunken face, and `parse_css` keys them separately. The appended group sits later than the landed `button:backdrop:active, button:backdrop:checked` block, so on a backdrop checked hover the restated sunken face wins that equal-specificity tie too — consistent with the landed disabled/backdrop entry's policy that backdrop never varies the face. No geometry, artwork, padding or dependency change; no other rule in either sheet is touched. In `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, add `TestGtk4Theme::test_button_checked_hover_and_active` beside `test_button_disabled_and_backdrop` (test anchoring, not a line number), asserting `assert_rule("button:checked:hover", {"background-image": "none", "border-color": BLACK, "box-shadow": INVERTED_BUTTON_BEVEL, "color": BLACK})` and the identical dict for `"button:checked:active"` (reusing the landed constants so the test stays tied to the landed face). In `docs/invariants.md`, append one row under `## gtk` naming `test_button_checked_hover_and_active`, the missing-reference provenance, the GTK 4 and GTK 3 probes (GTK 3 naming the negative result) and the declaration-only coverage.

**Acceptance criteria.** Both stock selectors' hover and press repaints resolve to the landed sunken face: the sheet declares `button:checked:hover` and `button:checked:active` with exactly the landed `button:active, button:checked` face values, `make check` passes including the two new-argument dict assertions, the invariants row is present, the GTK 3 sheet is byte-unchanged, and `grep` still finds no sheet rule with a `notebook … arrow` or other new selector.

**Scope boundary.** The grouped `notebook > header > tabs > arrow:checked:hover` / `arrow:checked:active` members of the same stock rules stay out — the GTK 4 sheet declares no tab-header scroll-arrow rules at all, and clearing them means inventing the arrow family's whole treatment, a candidate plan of its own. The next residue the same landed disabled/backdrop entry reserves is the `-gtk-icon-filter: brightness(1.2)` on stock's `button:hover` arm (Default-light.css, the same probe), a candidate plan of its own; the landed `pathbar`, `stackswitcher` and `tab` checked-hover surface rules this entry must not touch stay landed as they are. The three `BUGS.md ## Open` entries stay `[blocked: needs review]` with the bugfix role.

### Platinum GTK paned handles: restate the stock selected, wide and direction arms in both sheets with the landed etched recipe (planned 2026-10-31 by the plan role; independent of the waiting GTK 4 scale-popup entry — both touch `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` and `docs/invariants.md`, but every edit appends text: this entry appends one paned block at the tail of the GTK 4 sheet after the landed `.osd scale > trough > slider:disabled` block plus whichever scale-popup rules that entry has added by then, and one paned block at the tail of `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css` after the landed scale-popup rules; a paned selector never carries `scale-popup`, no test function overlaps (`test_paned_handle` and the landed background-image test stay each other's neighbours and this entry adds its own tests beside them), and both sheets feed one single appended `## gtk` invariants row, so either merge order leaves the cascade and the table right; re-filed 2026-10-31 by the plan role from ## Done, where it was stranded unstamped with nothing implemented anywhere (grep: no `paned … separator:dir` rule in either sheet, no `test_paned_handle_stock_clearances` in either suite and no `## gtk` row naming the direction arms); independent of the re-filed push-button entry above — every edit appends tail text, its `test_paned_handle_stock_clearances` is new beside the landed `test_paned_handle`/`test_paned_handle_background_images` pair while that entry's `test_button_disabled_and_backdrop` is new beside `test_button_focus_transition`, and their invariants rows are each their own, so either queue order leaves the cascade and the tables right) — done 2026-11-02 by the clean role
— done 2026-10-31 by the feature role


**Goal.** Keep the landed 1px etched split handle on every `paned` arm the stock theme still paints: a selected handle must not show the stock blue fill, a `wide-handle` paned must not grow the stock 5px grey grip or its twin `#CDC7C2` grip images, and a horizontal paned's handle must not reach back for the stock 8px gutter margins the landed orientation rules do not outrank.

**Grounding.** The landed GTK 4 rules `paned.horizontal > separator` and `paned.vertical > separator` in `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` (pinned by `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::TestGtk4Theme::test_paned_handle` through the shared `assert_paned_handles` helper and the `PANED_HANDLE_*` dicts in `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py`) declare the etched face with `margin: 0; padding: 0; -gtk-icon-source: none` but no `background-image`, no `:selected` arm, no `.wide` arm and no `:dir` arm. Probed with `gresource` on 2026-10-31 from `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Default/Default-light.css` in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-4.so.1` (libgtk-4 4.18.6), the stock GTK 4 arms the landed rules leave live are `paned > separator` declaring `… background-image: image(#cdc7c2); background-size: 1px 1px;`, `paned > separator:selected` declaring `background-image: image(#3584e4)`, `paned > separator.wide` declaring `min-width: 5px; min-height: 5px; background-color: #f6f5f4; background-image: image(#cdc7c2), image(#cdc7c2); …`, and the direction arms `paned.horizontal > separator:dir(ltr)` declaring `margin: 0 -8px 0 0; padding: 0 8px 0 0;` with `paned.horizontal > separator:dir(rtl)` its mirror — each `:dir` arm carries one class more than the landed `paned.horizontal > separator` rule, so it wins the margin and padding cascade regardless of sheet order; the landed GTK 4 etch inherits this residue from the landed GTK 3 etch, whose stock counterpart in `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css` of libgtk-3 3.24.49 declares the identical 8px `:dir` arms (same probe names), and the landed sheets clear the equal-specificity vertical margin and the wide geometry by sheet order, so the two `:dir` horizontal arms are the only margins a tie cannot decide. GTK 4 carries no `paned > separator:backdrop` arm — that arm is GTK 3-only — and the GTK 3 side needs only the direction clearance: its stock images on base, selected, backdrop, `.wide` and `.wide:backdrop` are already cleared by the landed group pinned by `tests/test_gtk_theme_views.py::TestGtkThemeViews::test_paned_handle_background_images`, each of whose five selectors is the exact stock twin and wins by sheet order. No reference screenshot shows a GTK split pane, so the etch stays the landed reference-grounded pair pinned by `tests/test_desktoptheme_line.py::TestLineReference` and these restatements are a platform adaptation recorded under today's date.

**Approach and files.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, append at the sheet tail after the landed `.osd scale > trough > slider:disabled` block (and after any scale-popup rules a merged entry has added) one dated (2026-10-31) adaptation comment naming the missing split-pane reference, the two gresource probes above and the `tests/test_desktoptheme_line.py::TestLineReference` etch as the value source, followed by two rules: a `paned > separator, paned > separator:selected, paned > separator.wide` group declaring exactly `background-image: none` (each selector is the exact stock twin, so the landed sheet-order-tie convention decides), and a `paned.horizontal > separator:dir(ltr), paned.horizontal > separator:dir(rtl)` group declaring exactly `margin: 0; padding: 0` (the landed orientation rules' own values). In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, append at the sheet tail after the landed scale-popup rules the same dated adaptation comment, naming the direction residue and stating that GTK 3's backdrop, selected and wide images are already cleared by the landed `test_paned_handle_background_images` group, followed by one `paned.horizontal > separator:dir(ltr), paned.horizontal > separator:dir(rtl)` rule declaring exactly `margin: 0; padding: 0`. In `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, add `TestGtk4Theme::test_paned_handle_stock_clearances` beside `test_paned_handle`: with `assert_rule`, each of `paned > separator`, `paned > separator:selected` and `paned > separator.wide` equals `{"background-image": "none"}` and each of `paned.horizontal > separator:dir(ltr)` and `paned.horizontal > separator:dir(rtl)` equals `{"margin": "0", "padding": "0"}` (no new `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py` constant and no edit to the landed `assert_paned_handles`). In `tests/test_gtk_theme_views.py`, add `TestGtkThemeViews::test_paned_handle_direction_margins` beside `test_paned_handle_background_images`, asserting the same two `:dir` selectors equal `{"margin": "0", "padding": "0"}`. Append one row to the `## gtk` invariants table in `docs/invariants.md` naming both new tests (the GTK 3 landed image-clearance row stays untouched), the index-date probes and the declaration-only coverage.

**Acceptance criteria.** Removing either appended rule or any of its selectors or declarations, or renaming a selector to anything but its exact stock twin, fails the new test that pins it. The landed `test_paned_handle` in both suites, `test_paned_handle_background_images`, `test_no_universal_selector` and `test_only_palette_hex_literals` stay green: the appended blocks add no hex literal and no universal selector. No artwork, geometry, metric or dependency changes; the landed paned rules, the landed GTK 3 image group, the scale-popup entry's selectors and every other surface stay outside this plan. Run `make check`. It merges before or after the waiting GTK 4 scale-popup entry in either order.

### Platinum GTK push buttons: restate the stock insensitive and backdrop face recolours (planned 2026-10-31 by the plan role; independent of the waiting message-dialog entry — both entries append groups at the tail of `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` and `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, but this entry's selectors never carry a `dialog` or `message` token, its test functions (`test_button_disabled_and_backdrop` in each suite) are new beside `test_button_focus_transition`, it appends its own single `## gtk` invariants row, and dialog selectors never match a plain push button in any state, so either merge order leaves the cascade right; re-filed 2026-10-31 by the plan role from ## Done, where it was stranded unstamped with nothing implemented anywhere (grep: no `button:disabled`, `button:backdrop` or any compound of the two in either sheet, no `test_button_disabled_and_backdrop` in either suite and no `## gtk` row naming them); independent of the re-filed paned-handles entry below — both append tail groups with disjoint selectors (a plain `button`-state selector never carries `paned`), disjoint new tests beside each other's neighbours and their own `## gtk` invariants rows, so either queue order leaves the cascade right) — done 2026-11-02 by the clean role
— done 2026-10-31 by the feature role

**Goal.** A push button must keep the landed Platinum raised face in its insensitive and unfocused states: a disabled button must not repaint itself off-white with a greyed label, and a button inside an unfocused window must not lose its bevel to a flat off-white face.

**Grounding.** Neither `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` nor `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css` declares `button:disabled`, `button:backdrop` or any compound of the two (grep: the landed button state rules are `button`, `button:hover`, `button:active, button:checked` and `button:focus`/`:focus-visible` arms), and heading searches of this queue, `PLANS-DONE.md`, `BUGS.md` and `BUGS-FIXED.md` found no plain-button disabled or backdrop restatement (the landed OSD suggested- and destructive-action plans restate only `.osd button:disabled` inside overlays). Probed with `gresource` on 2026-10-31, the stock resources declare the surviving residues: from `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Default/Default-light.css` of `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-4.so.1` (libgtk-4 4.18.6) — `notebook > header > tabs > arrow:backdrop, button.backdrop.flat, button:backdrop`-grouped arms declaring `color: #929595; border-color: #d5d0cc; background-image: image(#f6f5f4); box-shadow: none; transition: 200ms ease-out` (its `button:backdrop.flat` member is left alone below), `button:backdrop:active, button:backdrop:checked` with `background-image: image(#e9e9e3); box-shadow: none`, `button:backdrop:disabled` with `color: #d4cfca; background-image: image(#faf9f8)`, `button:backdrop:disabled:active, button:backdrop:disabled:checked` with `image(#e9e9e3)`, `button:disabled` with `color: #929595; border-color: #d5d0cc; background-image: image(#faf9f8); -gtk-icon-filter: opacity(0.5)`, and `button:disabled:active, button:disabled:checked` with `image(#e9e9e3); box-shadow: none`; from `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css` of `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0` (libgtk-3 3.24.49) the same six shapes with GTK 3's own colour set (`#e4e4e0` pressed, `#cdc7c2` borders, `inset 0 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0)` box shadows and `text-shadow: none`/`-gtk-icon-shadow: none` resets the cascade keeps applying). Each stock `button…` member outranks or ties the landed face groups it must lose to, so no sheet-order tie decides these without restatement. No collected reference screenshot shows a disabled GTK widget (the sheet header records the insensitive-adaptation convention), so the disabled label reuses the recorded insensitive grey `#888888` — Kvantum's own `disabled.text.color` and the landed `label:disabled, text:disabled, spinbutton.vertical > text:disabled` grey on GTK 4 and `label:disabled, entry:disabled, spinbutton:disabled` on GTK 3 — and the backdrop states restate the landed `button` group's raised bevel, landed `button:active, button:checked` sunken bevel and landed black border; the stock `transition: 200ms ease-out` on the GTK 3 and GTK 4 backdrop arms is restated to `none` because the landed `button` group states `transition: none` (pinned by `test_button_focus_transition` through the shared scale policy). The stock `-gtk-icon-filter: opacity(0.5)` on `button:disabled` stays in force: no landed value records an icon-dimming treatment and the stock fade parallels the greyed label (recorded as a kept toolkit value, not cleared).

**Goal.** The landed Platinum OSD overlay band (`theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, the restated `.osd .scale-popup, … toolbar.osd` container painted `#DDDDDD`) fields its spinbuttons with the landed entry-field arms — the restated `.osd spinbutton:not(.vertical)`, `:focus`, `:backdrop` and `:disabled` group — but its stepper buttons still draw the stock claims: the horizontal stepper base arm paints a transparent face clipped of every visual claim except a left-edge separator (`border-style: none none none solid`, `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4)`), a near-white `#eeeeec` icon and nine `0 1px black` icon-shadow pair, its `:hover` arm a translucent `rgba(238, 238, 236, 0.1)` bubble with the same border claims, its `:backdrop` and `:disabled` arms transparent faces with grey `#919190` disabled icons — all invisible on the light band — and each edge arm rounds a stock 5px corner (`border-radius: 0 5px 5px 0` on `:dir(ltr):last-child`, `5px 0 0 5px` on `:dir(rtl):first-child`), while the vertical family paints full stock dark faces (`image(rgba(53, 53, 53, 0.9))` base and `:backdrop`, `rgba(83, 83, 83, 0.9)` on hover, `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7)` active, `rgba(71, 71, 71, 0.5)` disabled) with `#eeeeec`/`white` icons, a `0 1px black` shadow pair, an `rgba(238, 238, 236, 0.3)` outline and a `background-clip: padding-box` claim — everything other than a Platinum button on the light band. Restate the stock arms with the landed plain push-button recipe so a spinbutton's steppers inside a restated overlay draw the restated coherent unit: the landed `#FFFFFF` entry-field face beside raised `#DDDDDD` push-button faces in every stock state; the stock dark-bubble stepper distinction vanishes inside the overlays exactly as the landed plain, flat, suggested-action and queued destructive-action restatements erased theirs.

**Approach and files.** No collected reference screenshot shows a GTK OSD overlay or a spinbutton inside one; this is the same platform adaptation the landed container, entry, check/radio, meter, scale-thumb, thin-bar, push-button, flat-button and suggested-action plans made — reuse the landed recipe, record the stock claims the restatement overrides. The recipe comes from `tests/support/gtk_rule_cases.py::GtkSharedControlCases::test_button` (the landed "flat"-family dictionaries `tests/test_gtk_theme_osd.py::TestGtkThemeOsd::test_osd_button` and `test_osd_suggested_action` compose) and the `FACE`, `BLACK`, `BUTTON_BEVEL`, `INVERTED_BUTTON_BEVEL` and `ETCH_DARK` specs in `tests/support/platinum_palette.py` and `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py`, taken directly so this entry needs nothing from any queued entry to land. The stock arms come from `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css` in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0` (libgtk-3 3.24.49, extracted with `gresource`, probed 2026-10-30: seven horizontal rules — `.osd spinbutton:not(.vertical) button` alone with each of `:dir(rtl)`, `:hover`, `:backdrop`, `:disabled`, `:dir(ltr):last-child` and `:dir(rtl):first-child` — and five vertical rules — `.osd spinbutton.vertical button:first-child` alone with each of `:hover`, `:active`, `:disabled` and `:backdrop`; twelve rules, twelve selectors) — re-probe the resource and re-derive every stock claim before writing.

(1) In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, append a dated provenance comment and the twelve restated rules directly after the sheet's last restated `.osd` block (on the 2026-10-30 planning date that is the landed `.osd button.suggested-action:active:backdrop, …` block closing the sheet; should the queued destructive-action restatement land first, after whichever restated block is then last) at the stock spellings in the stock rule order — horizontal base, `:dir(rtl)`, `:hover`, `:backdrop`, `:disabled`, `:dir(ltr):last-child`, `:dir(rtl):first-child`, then vertical base, `:hover`, `:active`, `:disabled`, `:backdrop` — so each appends after its stock twin at equal specificity and pre-empts exactly the stock arm it restates. Each restated arm declares byte-equal the landed flat-and-push-button dictionary — `background-color: #DDDDDD` (`FACE`), `background-image: none`, `border: 1px solid #000000`, `border-radius: 0`, `box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #AAAAAA` (`BUTTON_BEVEL`), `color: #000000` (`BLACK`), `outline-color: #000000`, `text-shadow: none`, `-gtk-icon-shadow: none` — except: the `:hover` arms repeat the base recipe byte-equal (they must defeat the stock hover's bubble and dark face); the vertical `:active` arm swaps only `box-shadow` to the landed inverted bevel `inset 1px 1px #AAAAAA, inset -1px -1px #FFFFFF` (`INVERTED_BUTTON_BEVEL`; the horizontal stock set carries no active arm — pressed steppers take the hover underline in stock, so nothing to restate there); the two `:disabled` arms keep the base bevel with the Inactive grey `color: #888888` (`ETCH_DARK`, the stock `#919190` cleared) and no `outline-color`, as every landed disabled arm claims none; and the `:backdrop` arms repeat the base recipe byte-equal, recipe `outline-color` included. Record in the provenance comment the claims the restatement erases: the stock `:dir(rtl)` separator flip (`border-style: none solid none none`) and the base arm's right-side separator (`border-style: none none none solid` over `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4)`, the hover's `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)` variant) — both cleared by the recipe's full four-sided black border so a stepper draws identically in both directions; the two stock 5px edge radii on `:dir(ltr):last-child`/`:dir(rtl):first-child` — cleared by the recipe's `border-radius: 0`, byte-equal base restatements on both arms; the vertical family's `rgba(238, 238, 236, 0.3)` `outline-color` — restated black, as the landed `.osd` check/radio arms did; and the vertical family's `background-clip: padding-box` — the one clearance stock's own claims force here, as the landed suggested-action restatement's: every vertical stock arm claims `padding-box`, which left standing would clip the `#DDDDDD` face, so each restated vertical arm declares `background-clip: border-box` and the comment records it. The horizontal stock arms claim no `background-clip`, so the restated horizontal arms omit the property, exactly as the landed flat-button blocks stayed omitted. Leave undeclared so geometry keeps governing: `button.osd`'s `min-width: 26px; min-height: 32px` and `min-width: 34px` image-button arm (they never match a spinbutton leftmiddle stepper and are recorded as untouched), the `.osd spinbutton:not(.vertical) entry` `min-width: 28px` inner-entry rule, and the landed entry-field arms themselves.

(2) In `tests/test_gtk_theme_osd.py`, add `TestGtkThemeOsd::test_osd_spinbutton_buttons` beside the landed `test_osd_suggested_action`: build three expected dictionaries from the imported specs — the base button dictionary above, the disabled dictionary `{**base, "color": ETCH_DARK}` minus `"outline-color"`, and the active dictionary `{**base, "box-shadow": INVERTED_BUTTON_BEVEL}` — and build the horizontal variants of each so its dictionary omits `"background-clip"` while each vertical dictionary carries the literal `"background-clip": "border-box"`; assert each of the twelve selectors — the seven single-selector horizontal rules and five single-selector vertical rules listed in (1), no comma list in this family — against the right dictionary. Add the scope assertion that the set of parsed sheet selectors carrying the substring `spinbutton` plus the substring ` button` (an underscoreless, space-prefixed match that separates the stepper node from the spinbutton and entry node spellings — the bare `button` token is useless here because `spinbutton` contains it) plus one of the `.osd`, `app-notification`, `touch-selection` or `magnifier` tokens equals exactly that enumerated twelve — grep-verified 2026-10-30 that no landed sheet selector pairs a `spinbutton` and a stepper `button` spelling (the only hits for either pair in today's sheet are provenance-comment lines inside queued-entry records) — so the scan kills dupes and stray variants. In the same change, extend `test_osd_entry_fields`' existing exact-set sweep — selectors carrying `.osd entry` or `.osd spinbutton` — with the same `" button" not in selector` exclusion so the stepper selectors stay out of that landed test's exact-set (the sweep keeps enumerating today's four field comma lists: `test_osd_entry_fields`' four pairs `.osd spinbutton:not(.vertical)`/`.osd entry` through `:disabled`), mirroring the landed push-button plan's `button`-token exclusion in `test_osd_overlay_bands`'s filter, which already clears this entry's twelve selectors since each carries the `button` token; no change beyond that one sweep line to `test_osd_overlay_bands`, `test_osd_button`, `test_osd_flat_button`, `test_osd_suggested_action` or any other landed scope enumeration.

(3) In `docs/invariants.md`, in the `## gtk` table, append one row following the row pinned by `test_osd_suggested_action`: the guarantee — every stock GTK 3 spinbutton stepper (`:first-child` up and down steppers in the horizontal and vertical `.osd spinbutton` node arms) inside the restated Platinum OSD overlay band draws the landed push-button face (`#DDDDDD`, full black square border and bevel, zero radius, black label, grey `#888888` insensitive label, inverted bevel where the stock arms claim a pressed state) in every stock state, the stock dark-bubble and separator/edge-radius claims erased inside overlays as the plain, flat and suggested-action restatements erased theirs — with the test column naming `tests/test_gtk_theme_osd.py::TestGtkThemeOsd::test_osd_spinbutton_buttons`, the provenance cell naming the missing reference surface, the gresource probe, the recipe reuse, the erased stock claims and the cleared vertical `background-clip: padding-box` claim (restated `border-box`, matching the suggested-action adaptation), and the declaration-checks note the neighbouring landed rows carry.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Each of the twelve enumerated selectors parses to the recipe dictionary its arm maps to; the dictionaries differ only where the recipe itself differs — `color` on the two disabled arms, `box-shadow` on the vertical `:active` arm, `outline-color` absent on the disabled arms, and `background-clip` present only on the vertical arms.
- The scope assertion enumerates exactly the twelve restated selectors and nothing else; `test_osd_overlay_bands`, `test_osd_button`, `test_osd_flat_button`, `test_osd_suggested_action` and every landed `.osd` scope enumeration still pass with no change at all, and `test_osd_entry_fields` still enumerates exactly its four field comma lists.
- The sheet's added block sits after the sheet's last restated `.osd` block on the implementation date; no landed rule in the sheet is touched, and the `.osd button.color colorswatch`, `.osd .scale-popup button.flat`, `.scale-popup button:hover` and `colorchooser .popover.osd` arms stay queued (recorded here, not this change); the generic spinbutton stepper arms outside `.osd` keep governing outside overlays, as do `.osd spinbutton:not(.vertical) entry` and the two `button.osd` geometry minimum arms.
- One new `## gtk` invariants row names the missing reference surface, the toolkit probe, the recipe reuse, the erased stepper distinction and the cleared clip claim.
- `make check` is green.

Size: twelve restated rules (twelve selectors) plus one test (with the `test_osd_entry_fields` sweep line recorded above) plus one invariants row and no other filter change — a single implementation run's worth of change; the colorswatch, `.scale-popup` flat and `colorchooser .popover.osd` arms are queued separately after this entry lands.

  border-radius: 0;

### Theme apply: separate optional integrations from required selections (planned 2026-11-01 by the organize role) — done 2026-11-02 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Clarify ownership in `tools/apply_theme.py`: its required selection loop is part of applying the installed theme, while `_run_best_effort`, `_select_kvantum_theme` and `_reconfigure_kwin` each implement optional external integrations with distinct missing-tool and failure policies. Keeping the optional command policy beside orchestration obscures which failures can change the apply status.

**Approach and files.** Keep `tools/apply_theme.py` responsible for CLI parsing, required selections, locking, scratch lifetime and exit status. Move `_run_best_effort`, `_select_kvantum_theme` and `_reconfigure_kwin` into a focused `tools/theme_apply_optional.py`, along with their optional tool constants and imports; expose one function that performs the optional selections in the existing Kvantum-then-KWin order. Preserve the current note wording, timeout/log names, return status and direct-script/package import behavior. Update `tests/test_apply_theme.py` and any direct helper references, then search source, tests and markdown for stale ownership references. Files: `tools/apply_theme.py`, new `tools/theme_apply_optional.py`, relevant apply tests, and `docs/invariants.md` only if the documented ownership needs correction.

**Acceptance criteria.** The optional commands still run under the existing data-home lock and scratch directory, after all required selections; either optional tool being missing, failing to start, timing out or exiting nonzero remains a note and leaves apply status unchanged. Existing command order, arguments, diagnostics and log filenames remain the same. Unit coverage exercises the extracted boundary, direct-script and package imports work, and `make check` passes.

### Reference-pixel sampler: locate emitted histogram colors (planned 2026-11-02 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-02 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Show where dominant palette colors occur without a separate `--find-color` invocation per color. `tools/sample_reports.py::report` emits histogram counts, while its find-color branch computes bounds for one selected RGB predicate. `tools/sample_arguments.py::build_parser` has no histogram-bounds option. Source option searches and related planned/archived sampler entries cover counts, top-color limits, single-color lookup and alpha grouping, rather than per-histogram-color bounds. This is independent of the queued fidelity budget.

**Approach and files.** Add boolean `--color-bounds` in `tools/sample_arguments.py::build_parser`; in `tools/sample.py::main`, reject it without `--histogram` with status 2 and empty stdout before image reads. In `tools/sample_reports.py::report`, keep the existing counting and sorted/top-color selection, then, only when requested, scan the decoded region once more to accumulate min/max coordinates for the emitted color keys. Reuse `_positioned_region_pixels` and, for `--alpha`, `_region_alpha`: RGB mode groups opacity variants together; alpha mode uses exact RGBA keys, including uncomposited RGB beneath transparency and opaque fallback 255. Retain bounds state only for emitted keys, without lists of matching pixels or additional image reads. Each emitted JSON color gains `bounds: {"x": X, "y": Y, "width": W, "height": H}`; append `  bounds=X,Y,W,H` after the existing text color fields. Bounds use absolute image coordinates and enclose disconnected occurrences within the requested region; they do not imply a solid rectangle. Keep ordering, counts, top-color summaries and omitted-option output intact. Add `tests/test_sample_histogram_bounds.py` using `support.cli_fixtures.CliTestCase` and `support.png_fixtures`, document the option in README.md's sampling section, and add a dated tooling guarantee in `docs/invariants.md`. These six files bound one run; no dependency, decoder or theme-art changes are needed.

**Acceptance criteria.** Independently specified fixtures assert text and JSON bounds for a single pixel, a uniform region, and disconnected occurrences whose extrema lie on different rows. A crop with nonzero origins in both axes excludes same-colored outside pixels and reports absolute coordinates. Cover tied counts and `--top-colors 1`, limits at/above the distinct count, unchanged summaries, RGB grouping across opacity variants, RGBA separation at alpha 0/128/255, preserved transparent RGB and opaque fallback. Without the flag, existing histogram output remains covered by its regressions. Misuse with plain sampling, runs or find-color returns 2 with empty stdout before header or row reads. Assert one bounded PNG decode, direct-script JSON and help text; a helper spy should show the additional bounds traversal is skipped without the flag. Run `make check` after the final implementation/documentation edit.

### Fidelity gate: cap the worst channel delta alongside aggregate budgets (planned 2026-11-02 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-02 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Allow an aggregate error budget to tolerate small differences while rejecting an isolated severe error. `tools/fidelity_metrics.py::Metrics.max_delta` already reports the worst absolute channel delta; `tools/fidelity_reports.py::budget_verdict` now gates it alongside MAE, differing fraction and RMSE. The RMSE budget remains supported.

**Implementation.** Added `--max-delta N` with ASCII integer validation from 0 through 255. The gate combines each supplied budget, uses the already computed raw RGBA maximum, and keeps default output unchanged when omitted. JSON records `thresholds.max_delta`; text displays the cap before tolerance. Added CLI coverage, documented raw alpha and transparent RGB behavior in README.md, and updated the fidelity invariant. Verification: `make check` passed after the final edits.

### Fidelity gate: accept an explicit RMSE budget (planned 2026-11-02 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-02 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Let a comparison constrain concentrated channel errors with the root mean square error already computed by `tools/fidelity_metrics.py::compare`. `tools/fidelity.py::main` exposes MAE and differing-fraction budgets; `tools/fidelity_reports.py::budget_verdict` checks those two metrics, while `render_text` already prints RMSE. Searches for `max-rmse` and RMSE-budget terms in source, tests and planned/archived entries found no such gate. This is independent of the waiting sampler alpha-filter plan.

**Approach and files.** Add `--max-rmse F` to `tools/fidelity.py::main`, with a `max_rmse` validator in `tools/fidelity_arguments.py` reusing `_finite_float` and `_channel_amount` to accept finite plain ASCII numbers in 0..255. Extend `tools/fidelity_reports.py::budget_verdict` with an optional trailing `max_rmse=None` parameter: compare the existing full-precision `metrics.rmse <= max_rmse`, require each supplied budget to pass, and use the current no-differing-pixel fallback only when no budget is supplied. Pass the new value by keyword. Extend `report_data` with a defaulted keyword parameter without moving existing positional parameters; add `thresholds.max_rmse` only when supplied. In `render_text`, insert `max-rmse=F` formatted to four decimals before `tolerance=` on the verdict line only when supplied. Preserve omitted-option text and JSON shapes. Update the CLI synopsis/help and README.md's Fidelity checking budget explanation: RMSE uses the existing raw channel bytes, including alpha as computed today, is independent of tolerance, and is not perceptual error. Add `tests/test_fidelity_rmse_budget.py` using `support.fidelity_cli_case.FidelityCliTestCase`, and update the aggregate-budget tooling row in `docs/invariants.md` with the implementation date. The run touched the six listed files; no metric computation, image decoder, render gate invocation or dependency changes were needed.

**Acceptance criteria.** Use independently calculated small PNG fixtures to show a sparse large error passing MAE but failing RMSE; an RMSE-only budget replaces the strict default; and combinations fail whenever any supplied budget fails. Pin exact equality and just-below thresholds with an exactly representable RMSE fixture, zero on identical/different images, and the upper bound 255. Cover alpha-only differences, opaque RGB inputs (the CLI decodes alpha), nonzero candidate/reference crops excluding an outside error, and tolerance 255 still allowing an RMSE-budget failure. Assert full-precision JSON threshold, matching text verdict/status, and omitted-option output compatibility with the existing schema and verdict line. Invalid negative, over-255, nonfinite, fractional-malformed, non-ASCII and missing values return 2 with empty stdout before image reads; ordinary decimal fractions remain valid. Exercise direct-script JSON invocation and help text. Expanded tests also pin MAE/RMSE interactions, exact threshold equality, raw transparent RGB, missing arguments and help output. Existing budget/report regressions stayed green under `make check`.

### Reference-pixel sampler: filter color-location bounds by exact alpha (planned 2026-11-02 by the plan role) — done 2026-11-02 by the feature role

**Goal and grounding.** Locate a color's visible or transparent artwork bounds without merging pixels of different opacity. `tools/sample_reports.py::report` currently searches RGB alone; `tools/sample.py::main` decodes alpha only for `--alpha`, which it rejects with `--find-color`. Searches of sampler source/tests and planned/archived headings found RGB color location, RGB tolerance, and alpha-aware samples/runs/histograms, but no alpha filter for color location. This is independent of the queued fidelity diagnostic.

**Approach and files.** Add optional `--match-alpha N` in `tools/sample_arguments.py::build_parser`, accepting a plain ASCII integer from 0 through 255 using the existing numeric-validation conventions. In `tools/sample.py::main`, reject explicit use without `--find-color` before image reads, including zero, and request bounded `read_png(..., alpha=True)` when the filter is supplied. Retain the existing `--alpha --find-color` rejection: this new option supplies a search predicate rather than changing sample output. In the find-color branch of `tools/sample_reports.py::report`, traverse `_region_alpha` alongside `_region_pixels` when requested and count a pixel only when its alpha equals N and its RGB satisfies the existing color-tolerance predicate. Missing alpha is 255; preserve RGB beneath transparency without compositing. **Approach and files.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, append a dated (2026-10-31) provenance comment naming the probe and the missing flat reference surface after whichever landed rule is last in the sheet at merge time (on the plan date that is the landed `button.destructive-action:focus:focus-visible` block), followed by the eight grouped restatements, each selector its exact stock twin (equal class-token count, later source order wins every tie, and each arm's stock claim namespace per state is covered because every higher-token stock spelling above is restated):

1. `button.flat` — base raised recipe: `background-color: #DDDDDD; background-image: none; border: 1px solid #000000; border-radius: 0; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #AAAAAA; transition: none;` (the `background-color` and `border` shorthand must be declared because stock claims `background-color: transparent` and `border-color: transparent` here; the full recipe, not face-only, follows the landed `.osd` flat precedent of repeating the raised recipe wherever stock claims shadowless flat faces).
2. `button.flat:hover` — the same full base recipe again (`transition: none` instead of the landed hover's face-only shape, because stock's hover arm claims a transparent border-color, `box-shadow: none` and a 500ms transition that outrank them at the landed groups' shape).
3. `button.flat:active, button.flat:checked, button.flat.keyboard-activating` — stock's pressed-arm grouping with the sunken recipe: `background-color: #DDDDDD; background-image: none; border: 1px solid #000000; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #AAAAAA, inset -1px -1px #FFFFFF; transition: none;` (the same the landed `button:active, button:checked` group swaps plus the stock-claimed properties the raised neighbors must be beaten).
4. `button.flat:backdrop, button.flat:disabled, button.flat:backdrop:disabled` — the landed disabled shape: `background-color: #DDDDDD; background-image: none; border: 1px solid #000000; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #AAAAAA; color: #888888;` (stock claims `background-color: transparent` and a transparent border-color here).
5. `button:backdrop.flat` — the base raised recipe plus `color: #000000` (stock's dark-on-light face and greyed label are the only leftover claims here; `background-color` inherits the landed `button` base).
6. `button:backdrop.flat:active, button:backdrop.flat:checked` — the sunken recipe plus `color: #000000` and `transition: none`.
7. `button:backdrop.flat:disabled` and 8. `button:backdrop.flat:disabled:active, button:backdrop.flat:disabled:checked` — the landed disabled shape of item 4 (greyed label from stock's `#d4cfca` denied).

In `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, add `TestGtk4Theme::test_flat_button_arms` beside `test_button_disabled_and_backdrop`: import the shared constants (`FACE`, `BUTTON_BEVEL`, `INVERTED_BUTTON_BEVEL` — the landed names of `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py` used through `assert_progressbar`'s own disabled arm work) and assert each new selector's dict (`BUTTON_BEVEL` on items 1–2, 4–8 and `INVERTED_BUTTON_BEVEL` on items 3 and 6, `FACE` background-color, the landed plain recipe's remaining literals) via `GtkSharedControlCases.assert_rule`-equivalent `self.rules[name]` exact-dict checks plus one `button.flat`-family inventory assertion (`{s for s in self.rules if s.startswith("button.flat") or s.startswith("button:backdrop.flat")}` equals the eight selectors), which fails when a stock spelling is skipped. Append one `## gtk` invariants row at the end of the `## gtk` section in `docs/invariants.md` naming the probe (Default-light.css, libgtk-4 4.18.6, 2026-10-31), the missing flat reference surface, and the eight selectors.

### Platinum GTK 4 plain suggested-action buttons: restate the stock blue family with the landed push-button recipe (planned 2026-10-31 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-31 by the feature role

**Goal.** A GTK 4 push button carrying the `suggested-action` class must draw the landed Platinum push-button face in every armed state — base, hover, press, checked, keyboard focus and disabled — instead of the stock blue gradient family.

**Grounding.** `grep -n "suggested" theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` matches only the landed square-pill container group at the sheet's mid-section, whose `menubutton.suggested-action.pill` member declares `border-radius: 0` and nothing else — no plain `button.suggested-action` state rule exists in the sheet, and no `PLANS.md ## Planned` entry, `PLANS-DONE.md` finished record, `BUGS.md`/`BUGS-FIXED.md` heading or `docs/invariants.md` row names the plain suggested-action family (the landed GTK 3 OSD suggested-action and destructive-action plans restated only the `.osd`-scoped arms; the landed plain disabled/backdrop plan's scope boundary reserves the plain variants as candidate plans of their own, confirmed by `PLANS-DONE.md`'s "families for later" record). Probed with `gresource` on 2026-10-31 from `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Default/Default-light.css` in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-4.so.1` (libgtk-4 4.18.6, extraction under a scratch dir), the stock plain family is: `button.suggested-action` with white text, `outline-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8)`, `border-color: #15539e`, a `linear-gradient` `background-image`, a `0 1px 2px` drop shadow and `transition-property`/`transition-duration: 300ms`; a second base arm with `outline: 0 solid transparent; outline-offset: 4px`; `button.suggested-action:focus:focus-visible` with `outline-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8); outline-width: 2px; outline-offset: -2px`; `button.suggested-action:hover` with a fresh gradient and `border-color: #185fb4`; `button.suggested-action:active, button.suggested-action:checked` with `image(#1961b9)`; `button.suggested-action:disabled` repainting to the stock greyed face `image(#faf9f8)` with `color: #929595`; and `button.suggested-action:disabled:active, button.suggested-action:disabled:checked` with `image(#2f80e3)`. Each of these selectors carries one class more than the landed `button`, `button:hover`, `button:active, button:checked`, `button:focus:focus-visible`, `button:backdrop…` and `button:disabled…` groups, so it outranks them and no sheet-order tie decides any arm. No collected reference screenshot shows a GTK suggested-action button at all (the GTK scope's standing adaptation premise), so each arm reuses the landed plain push-button recipe of the same sheet — the recipe precedent the landed `.osd button.suggested-action` plan set byte-for-byte follows, including the erased suggested colour distinction.

background-image: none; border-color: #000000; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #AAAAAA; color: #000000; outline-color: #000000; transition: none` (the base arm must restate `transition: none` because the stock base's 300ms outline animation outranks the landed `button` group's lower-specificity one); `button.suggested-action:hover` declaring exactly `background-color: #DDDDDD; background-image: none; border-color: #000000; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #AAAAAA; color: #000000; outline-color: #000000` (a hover arm needs the full recipe because the stock hover gradient and white text outrank the landed `button:hover` face group); `button.suggested-action:active, button.suggested-action:checked` declaring exactly `background-image: none; border-color: #000000; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #AAAAAA, inset -1px -1px #FFFFFF; color: #000000; outline-color: #000000` (the landed sunken face); `button.suggested-action:disabled, button.suggested-action:disabled:active, button.suggested-action:disabled:checked` declaring exactly `background-image: none; and `button.suggested-action:focus:focus-visible` declaring exactly `outline-color: #000000` beside the landed plain arm's own value. No geometry, artwork, padding or dependency change; no other rule in the sheet is touched.

In `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, add `TestGtk4Theme::test_suggested_action_plain_arms` beside `test_button_hover_icon_filter` (test anchoring, not a line number): with `assert_rule`, the restated dictionaries assert `self.rules["button.suggested-action"]` equals `{"background-color": FACE, "background-image": "none", "border-color": BLACK, "box-shadow": BUTTON_BEVEL, "color": BLACK, "outline-color": BLACK, "transition": "none"}`; `button.suggested-action:hover` equals the same dict without the `transition` key; `button.suggested-action:active` and `button.suggested-action:checked` equal `{"background-image": "none", "border-color": BLACK, "box-shadow": INVERTED_BUTTON_BEVEL, "color": BLACK, "outline-color": BLACK}` (the landed sunken-face constants from `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py`, so a change to the landed face must be mirrored here or the test fails); each of `button.suggested-action:disabled`, `button.suggested-action:disabled:active` and `button.suggested-action:disabled:checked` equals `{"background-image": "none", "border-color": BLACK, "box-shadow": BUTTON_BEVEL, "color": DISABLED_TEXT["color"]}`; and `button.suggested-action:focus:focus-visible` equals `{"outline-color": BLACK}` (the tie test also asserts it equals `self.rules["button:focus:focus-visible"]["outline-color"]`). ### Platinum GTK content-view surfaces: restate the stock base field on GTK 4 and clear the stock hover icon highlight in both sheets (planned 2026-10-31 by the plan role; independent of the landed GTK 4 push-button hover icon-filter entry (— done 2026-10-31, now in `## Done` below) — the entries touch `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` and `docs/invariants.md`, but every edit appends tail text or inserts beside a different neighbour: this entry appends its two GTK 4 `.content-view` blocks after that entry's `button:hover` block at the sheet tail, adds `TestGtk4Theme::test_content_view_field_and_hover` beside `test_view_background` while that entry adds its test beside `test_button_checked_hover_and_active`, appends one `.content-view:hover` block at the tail of `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css` that touches no `button` selector, adds `TestGtkTheme::test_content_view_hover` beside `test_content_view_background`, and appends its own `## gtk` invariants row; a `button:hover` tie and a `.content-view:hover` tie are decided independently in source order because no selector of either entry carries a token of the other, and the landed `test_content_view_background` counts only exact `.content-view` and `.content-view:backdrop` selectors, so either queue order leaves both cascades and the tables right)
— done 2026-10-31 by the feature role

**Goal.** A GTK container carrying the `content-view` class (GTK's `GtkIconView` and grid-style content containers add that class) must paint the landed Platinum white field in every state the toolkit repaints: on GTK 4 the shipped sheet names the class nowhere, so stock's grey field and its hovered-icon brightening both show; on GTK 3 the landed white base and backdrop group never covers stock's hover arm, so hovering an icon view still asks the toolkit to highlight the item icons.

**Grounding.** `grep -n "content-view" theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` matched nothing before the appended rules landed and now prints only the appended dated comment and the two `.content-view` blocks it added; before landing `grep -n "content-view:hover" theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css` printed the landed base group at `.content-view, .content-view:backdrop` only, so no hover arm existed in either sheet. Probed with `gresource` on 2026-10-31: `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Default/Default-light.css` in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-4.so.1` (libgtk-4 4.18.6) declares `.content-view { background-color: #e6e3e0; }` and a separate `.content-view:hover { -gtk-icon-filter: brightness(1.2); }` arm (its `.content-view:backdrop` arm does not exist — grep over the extracted resource shows no `:backdrop` compound), so both a grey container fill and a hover icon brightening take effect that the landed `.view, list` group only fixes for the plain view classes. `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css` in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0` (libgtk-3 3.24.49) declares the same base and a `.content-view:hover { -gtk-icon-effect: highlight; }` arm the landed GTK 3 group never touches, so hovering a GTK 3 icon view applies stock's separate icon-highlight effect (a property axis distinct from the `-gtk-icon-shadow` reset the landed GTK 3 push-button arm clearance already records and pins on `button`, proving the parser handles `-gtk-icon-effect`). No collected reference screenshot shows a GTK icon view or content-view container, so the base field reuses the landed white view field (pinned by `assert_view_background` through `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py::VIEW_BACKGROUND` and by the landed `TestGtkTheme::test_content_view_background`) and the two hover clearances follow the sheets' established `none` convention for stock interaction recolours on states no reference shows.

**Approach and files.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, append at the sheet tail (after the landed `button:checked:hover, button:checked:active` block and after any rules other entries have added since) one dated (2026-10-31) adaptation comment naming the missing content-view reference surface, the GTK 4 probe above and the landed `.view, list` group as the field source, then a `.content-view` rule declaring exactly `background-color: #FFFFFF; color: #000000;` — the stock twin selector ties stock's base grouping at equal specificity, so the appended later source order wins, and stock's `.content-view .tile` members carry their own selectors, which need nothing from this rule. Then `.content-view:hover` declaring exactly `-gtk-icon-filter: none`. In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, append at the sheet tail one equally dated comment naming the GTK 3 probe (base and backdrop already restated by the landed group, so only the hover axis survives here) and the landed GTK 3 push-button clearance as the `none` convention source, then a `.content-view:hover` rule declaring exactly `-gtk-icon-effect: none`. In `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, add `TestGtk4Theme::test_content_view_field_and_hover` beside `test_view_background`: `assert_rule(".content-view", VIEW_BACKGROUND)` (import `VIEW_BACKGROUND` from `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py`, already exported there and used through `GtkSharedControlCases::assert_view_background`) and `assert_rule(".content-view:hover", {"-gtk-icon-filter": "none"})`. In `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, add `TestGtkTheme::test_content_view_hover` beside `test_content_view_background`: `assert_rule(".content-view:hover", {"-gtk-icon-effect": "none"})`. Append one row at the end of the `## gtk` invariants table in `docs/invariants.md` naming both new tests, the two dated gresource probes, the missing reference surfaces and the declaration-only coverage stating the GTK 4 sheet gains its first content-view declarations while GTK 3 gains only the hover clearance.

**Acceptance criteria.** Deleting either appended rule, renaming a selector to anything but its exact stock twin (`.content-view` on GTK 4; `.content-view:hover` in both sheets) or changing any declared value fails the new test in the affected suite. The landed `test_view_background` (both suites), `test_content_view_background`, `test_button_text_and_icon_shadows`, `test_links`, `test_only_palette_hex_literals` and `test_no_universal_selector` stay green: the appended values reuse literals already in each sheet (`#FFFFFF`, `#000000`, `none`), add no universal selector, and the exact-dict expectations of `test_content_view_background` and the shared `assert_view_background` still hold because the new selectors are separate keys in `tests/support/gtk_css.parse_css`'s per-selector dictionaries. Run `make check`. It merges before or after any other waiting entry in either order.

**Scope boundary.** The stock `.content-view .tile` base and state arms (GTK 3 and GTK 4: `:active`, `:selected`, `:disabled`, the GTK 4-only `:backdrop`), the 32px `.content-view .tile check…`/`iconview.content-view.check…` tile-check family with its GTK 3 `:not(list)` variants (10 stock arms across both toolkits, the whole check treatment), the content-view rubber-band member selectors of the stock `rubberband` groups, GTK's `GtkFlowBox`/`GtkGridView` child classifications, and the disabled/backdrop label-grey reuse stay out — each a candidate plan of its own if a later inspection shows a residue. No artwork, geometry, metric or dependency change.

### Platinum GTK 4 OSD progress and scale arms: restate the stock dark trough, fill and progress paints with the landed progress-bar and scale recipes (planned 2026-10-30 by the plan role; independent of the waiting GTK 3 OSD progress-and-scale plan — it appends ten restated rules to `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, adds `TestGtk4Theme::test_osd_progress_scale` beside `test_osd_check_radio` in `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` and appends one row to the `## gtk` invariants table, while that entry edits the GTK 3 sheet, `tests/test_gtk_theme.py` and its own row; the only shared documents are `docs/invariants.md`, where each entry appends its own row, and `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py`, from which both import static specs and neither edits — no sheet selector, test function or suite overlaps; the landed GTK 3 OSD scale-thumb plan, `PLANS-DONE.md` entry "Platinum GTK 3 OSD scale thumbs", records the convention both meter plans follow: append-only edits at the sheet tail, so any merge order leaves the cascade correct) — done 2026-10-30 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed GTK 4 OSD container plan (`PLANS-DONE.md`, "Platinum
GTK 4 OSD overlay containers") and the landed GTK 4 OSD check/radio plan
repainted the GTK 4 sheet's stock OSD overlay containers and indicator
arms, but the GTK 4 sheet declares nothing for a progress bar or a scale
inside one (grep: the sheet's `osd` meters are only the landed bare
`progressbar.osd > trough` thin-bar adaptations at the landed
`test_progressbar_osd_trough_paint` and
`test_progressbar_osd_trough_thickness`, plus `.osd switch:checked`; no
rule whose selector carries `.osd` and a trough/fill/highlight/progress
node), so the toolkit resources' six `.osd` trough, fill and progress
paints supply translucent dark bubbles (`rgba(0,0,0,0.5)` foundations over
`rgba(0,0,0,0.7)` edges) inside Platinum OSD overlays
instead of the landed flat `#EEEEEE` trough face and flat `#CCCCFF`
progress fill. Restate all six paints with the landed GTK 4 progress-bar
and scale recipes, so a meter inside a Platinum OSD overlay draws like one
everywhere else.

**Verified facts (probed 2026-10-30, `gresource extract
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-4.so.1` of both
`/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Default/Default-light.css` and
`/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Default/Default-dark.css`, libgtk-4 4.18.6;
exhaustive scan of every rule in both resources whose selector contains
`osd` and one of `trough`/`fill`/`highlight`/`progress`).** Both resources
carry the identical six-paint inventory at `>`-child spellings: the base
group `.osd progressbar > trough, .osd scale > trough > fill, .osd scale
> trough` (`border-color: rgba(0,0,0,0.7)` plus
`background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0.5)`) and its `:disabled` sibling at the
same three selectors, which redeclares the trough paint with
`background-color: rgba(71,71,71,0.5)` in Default-light.css and
`rgba(58,58,57,0.5)` in Default-dark.css (the only value the two theme
variants disagree on — the restatement erases both); the base
progress/highlight group `.osd progressbar > trough > progress, .osd
scale > trough > highlight` (`border-color: rgba(0,0,0,0.7)`) and its
`:disabled` sibling at the same two selectors (`border-color:
transparent`); a bare `.osd scale > trough > fill` group
(`background-color: rgba(91,91,90,0.775)` — the value fill stock shows
over the dark trough, distinct from its trough-group paint); and the fill
clear `.osd scale > trough > fill:disabled` (`border-color: transparent`,
`background-color: transparent`). The trough and progress paints set no
geometry (no `min-*` or `margin`), no `-gtk-icon-source`, no `box-shadow`
and no `:backdrop` spelling; each grouped paint carries identical
declarations across the nodes it couples, so split at the landed recipe
boundaries, each split selector keeps its complete stock dictionary. No
stock `.osd` trough/fill/progress paint recolours anything else or
shadows. No collected reference screenshot shows a GTK OSD meter, so this
is a platform adaptation reusing the landed recipes — `PROGRESSBAR_TROUGH`,
`PROGRESSBAR_PROGRESS`, `SCALE_TROUGH` and `SCALE_EMPTY_FILL` in
`tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py` (the flat `#EEEEEE` trough face with the
1px black border, zero radius and `inset 1px 1px #999999` etch, the flat
`#CCCCFF` progress fill and the transparent fill/highlight face) — pinned
by the landed `GtkSheetRuleCases::assert_progressbar` and `assert_scale`
base cases via `TestGtk4Theme::test_progressbar` and
`TestGtk4Theme::test_scale` in `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, and the arm
selectors and state names are GTK-required (they spell the toolkit
resources' rules). The bare thin-bar trio (`.osd progressbar > trough`'s
distinct sibling group `progressbar.osd { min-width: 3px; ... }` and its
borderless trough and progress) stays out of scope — the landed
`progressbar.osd > trough` paint and orientation minimums keep governing

slider` dark-thumb arms, `.scale-popup button.flat` and the `button.osd`
families (recorded here as later surface plans, not this change).

**Approach and files.** (1) In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`,
append directly after the landed `.osd radio:disabled` face group (the
sheet's last block) a dated provenance comment naming the missing
reference surface, this `gresource` probe of both Default resources and
the reuse of the `PROGRESSBAR_*`/`SCALE_*` recipes, followed by ten
restated rules, each with one `>`-child stock selector and one recipe
(the landed sheet declares no disabled trough, fill or highlight arm of
its own, so every disabled arm repeats its landed base recipe
byte-for-byte, and the disabled progress fill matches the landed
`progressbar > trough > progress:disabled` colour):

```css
.osd progressbar > trough {
  background-color: #EEEEEE;
  background-image: none;
  border: 1px solid #000000;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #999999;
  min-height: 10px;
  min-width: 10px;
}
.osd scale > trough {
  background-color: #EEEEEE;
  background-image: none;
  border: 1px solid #000000;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #999999;
  min-height: 6px;
  min-width: 6px;
}
.osd scale > trough > fill,
.osd scale > trough > highlight {
  background-color: transparent;
  background-image: none;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: none;
  margin: 0;
}
.osd progressbar > trough > progress {
  background-color: #CCCCFF;
  background-image: none;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: none;
  margin: 0;
}
.osd progressbar > trough:disabled {
  background-color: #EEEEEE;
  background-image: none;
  border: 1px solid #000000;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #999999;
  min-height: 10px;
  min-width: 10px;
}
.osd scale > trough:disabled {
  background-color: #EEEEEE;
  background-image: none;
  border: 1px solid #000000;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #999999;
  min-height: 6px;
  min-width: 6px;
}
.osd scale > trough > fill:disabled,
.osd scale > trough > highlight:disabled {
  background-color: transparent;
  background-image: none;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: none;
  margin: 0;
}
.osd progressbar > trough > progress:disabled {
  background-color: #999999;
  background-image: none;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: none;
  margin: 0;
}
```

(that is eight rules covering ten selectors — the fill and highlight arms
share the face recipe, and their disabled arms share it too; spell each

button`/flat/suggested-action/destructive-action families for later

**Goal.** The landed Platinum OSD container band (`theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, the `.osd .scale-popup, … toolbar.osd` block painted `#DDDDDD` with black text) still gives a destructive-action button its own red-dark arms inside every restated overlay: the stock `.osd button.destructive-action` arm paints a translucent `rgba(224, 27, 36, 0.5)` red face with an `#eeeeec` label and a `0 1px black` text shadow, its `:hover` arm brightens the face and whitens the label, its `:active`/`:checked` arms go solid `#e01b24` red under a white label, and its `:disabled` and `:backdrop` arms carry grey and near-white labels over dark translucent faces — every state something other than a Platinum button on the light band. Restate the five stock arms with the landed plain push-button recipe so a destructive-action button inside a restated overlay draws the same raised face as every other button there; the stock red destructive distinction vanishes inside the overlays exactly as the landed plain, flat and push-button restatements erased theirs, and the provenance comment records that deviation.

The stock arms come from `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css` in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk-3.so.0` (libgtk-3 3.24.49, extracted with `gresource`, probed 2026-10-30: the five `button.destructive-action`-carrying `.osd` rules that follow the generic `button.destructive-action`/`.flat` block presentation — the `.osd button.destructive-action`, `.osd button.destructive-action:hover`, grouped `:active:backdrop, :active, :checked:backdrop, :checked`, grouped `:disabled:backdrop, :disabled` and `:backdrop` arms — nine selectors from five comma lists, stock faces `image(rgba(224, 27, 36, 0.5))`/`image(rgba(224, 27, 36, 0.7))`/`image(#e01b24)`, disabled face `image(rgba(71, 71, 71, 0.5))`, disabled label `#919190`) — re-probe the resource and re-derive every stock claim before writing. One stock claim is shared with the queued suggested-action arms and unique among the landed restatements: every one of the five arms carries `background-clip: padding-box` (the generic non-`.osd` `button.destructive-action` and `.flat` arms claim no clip). Left unstated it would survive the equal-specificity restatement and clip the `#DDDDDD` face to the padding box, so the restated face would no longer byte-match the restated plain buttons; each restated arm therefore declares `background-clip: border-box` to clear the stock clip, and the provenance comment records that cleared claim.

(1) In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, append a dated provenance comment and five restated rules directly after the sheet's last restated `.osd` button block (on the 2026-10-30 planning date that is the landed `.osd button.flat:active, .osd button.flat:checked` block that closes the sheet; should a queued sibling restatement land first, after whichever restated block is then last) at the stock spellings so they pre-empt exactly the stock arms they restate.
